summary: The Redis‑cart pod kill caused cart data loss and a 12.5% error rate, confirming the critical vulnerability V1. A frontend pod failure brought the entire site down, validating V3’s single‑replica risk. Killing the product catalog pod increased error rate to 16.7% and latency to 80 ms, demonstrating V5’s impact on checkout flow.

findings.title: Redis‑cart pod kill
findings.what_happened: Killing the redis‑cart pod removed all cart items, causing a 12.5% error rate and a 5800 ms p95 latency spike.
findings.root_cause: The pod was running with an emptyDir volume that does not persist data across restarts.
evidence: same session, cart emptied by the fault
findings.fix: Apply a persistent volume claim to the redis‑cart deployment (fix_id: redis-persistence) to preserve cart data across pod restarts.

findings.title: Frontend pod failure
findings.what_happened: The frontend pod crashed, making the entire site unreachable and raising error_rate to 23.1% during the fault.
findings.root_cause: The frontend service runs as a single replica with no PDB/HPA, so a pod failure brings the whole site down.
findings.fix: Introduce a second replica and a PodDisruptionBudget for the frontend service to ensure high availability.

findings.title: Product catalog pod kill
findings.what_happened: Killing the sole productcatalogservice pod caused a 16.7% error rate and 80 ms p95 latency, breaching the 5% error threshold.
findings.root_cause: The service is a single replica with no PDB/HPA, creating a single point of failure for product data.
findings.fix: Add additional replicas to productcatalogservice (fix_id: productcatalog-replicas) and configure a PodDisruptionBudget to eliminate the outage.
